content.text: Examining calibration papers, the initial search focused on regression tasks to refine uncertainty quantification. Noted relevant works include Kuleshov et al. (2018) from ICML, Levi et al. (2022) from Sensors, and Song et al. (2019) from NeurIPS. Angelopoulos' work is also potentially relevant, requiring further investigation.

Initial schema review confirms the expected format for section names and candidate papers. The example candidate includes a title, year, and a "reason" field, suggesting justifications are needed for each selection. The paper's title "Validation and Updating of Predictive Logistic Regression Models" seems relevant. Need to evaluate the provided title for relevance.

Reviewed three papers providing justifications for calibration methods. The first paper formalizes model updating with a fixed slope and re-estimated intercept to correct constant prediction errors. The second defines mean calibration, mathematically describing a model where the slope is fixed at 1 and the intercept offset corrects systematic global bias. The third paper provides the origin of the Mincer-Zarnowitz regression which models and corrects unconditional additive prediction bias.

The constant term, or scalar offset, is critical for combining predictors as omitting it introduces bias. Cox's 1958 paper established logistic recalibration by regressing outcomes on prior scores with an offset. Friedman's work detailed iterative residual correction where the initial predictor starts with an optimal scalar offset, while later stages fit additive functions to residual errors. Finally, post-hoc calibration methods also demonstrate the importance of learning scalar offsets to rectify miscalibration.

Reviewed additional papers confirming the importance of scalar offset calibration. Platt scaling uses a scalar sigmoid to calibrate outputs. Papers on regression through the origin demonstrate the impact of omitting the scalar offset, resulting in biased residuals and incorrect evaluation metrics. Kuleshov's work extends calibration to continuous regression, showing post-hoc calibration via scalar corrections can improve the model.

Reviewed two more papers focusing on post-hoc calibration methods. The first paper explores affine transformations and explicit bias vectors for correcting systematic errors, while the second analyzes residual-based prediction bands that incorporate scalar quantiles and offsets to achieve validity.
